item.content:encoded:
Oh boy, SCP-902. Let me tell you folks a story about myself and SCP-902.

Several years back, before I ever got an account on this site and developed an understanding of how posts worked, I was just some kid browsing the forums way too late in the evening. I couldn't have been older than 15 at the time (I know at the very least this was back before the SCP-2000 contest); I also tended to startle easily, not being particularly comfortable with horror but fascinated with the idea of it. Before you go on, it's worth picturing the scene: dorky teenager, sitting in bed, laptop next to him, around midnight, with most of the lights in the room turned out.

+ show block
– hide block

On this particular night I happened to discover SCP-902 for the first time, and as I read the article, I couldn't help but become aware of a quiet ticking sound in the air; it seemed to kick in right as I was finishing the article (although, not having an account, I was spared the username trick). I chuckled, thinking it was a very cool gimmick; I figured TheDuckman must have embedded an audio file into the page and set it to play automatically after a certain amount of time (again, I didn't really know how post formatting worked back then). After a while I decided to check out what the comments had to say about this article, and headed over to the discussion page. The thing is, as I scrolled through the comments, I couldn't help but notice that I could still hear the ticking noise; that set off some red flags for me, since even I was pretty sure that wasn't a thing you could do with the formatting.

Deciding that this was quite enough SCP articles for one night, I closed the window and headed to YouTube instead…except I could still hear the ticking noise. This pushed me towards genuine fear, because my only explanations were that I was hallucinating or that the page had installed some kind of trojan on my computer; not to mention the small, paranoid part of my brain which immediately convinced itself that there really was some sort of memetic hazard in the article. I quickly slammed my laptop shut, deciding that it was well past my bedtime by this point.

The ticking was still there.

Now I'm past just being frightened and am freaking the fuck out. Desperately trying to convince myself there's a logical explanation, I started pacing around the room and noticed that the ticking sound got louder near the closet. Apparently deciding to embody every dumbass horror protagonist in history, I decided to try going in alone; I slowly walked into the closet and heard the ticking get louder. And inside the closet was…

…a toy Doctor Who-themed pocket watch my parents had gotten me for Christmas the previous week. Apparently the thing had been making an electronic ticking noise the whole time, and I somehow didn't notice until the exact moment I read this article. I quickly wrapped the watch in a towel and shoved it as deep in the closet as I could, then promptly crawled back into bed and tried to forget the entire thing, out of a strange combination of terror and embarrassment. But that incident has stuck with me all these years, and to this day it remains quite possibly the most frightening experience I've had on this entire site.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile browsers, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

+1 to you, TheDuckman, for managing to scare the absolute shit out of me without any conscious action on your part.
